name: rmdir
title: Remove an empty directory
description: Deletes a directory only if it is already empty. This refusal to delete non-empty directories is the point - it is the safe counterpart to 'rm -r'.

flags.name: -p
flags.description: Remove the directory and any parent directories that become empty.

flags.name: --ignore-fail-on-non-empty
flags.description: Do not report an error when a directory is not empty.

examples.explanation: Deletes old_folder if it contains no files.
Removes c, then b, then a, stopping at the first non-empty one.

risk.sideEffects: Removes a directory entry from the filesystem.
risk.reversibility: Not recoverable through the shell, but only empty directories are affected.

name: dir
title: List directory contents on Windows
description: Lists files and subdirectories in a directory. This is the Windows Command Prompt equivalent of 'ls' and is a CMD built-in rather than a standalone executable.

flags.name: /a
flags.description: Include hidden and system files.

flags.name: /s
flags.description: Recurse into all subdirectories.

flags.name: /b
flags.description: Bare format - names only, no headings or summary.

examples.explanation: Lists the contents of the current directory.
Lists all entries including hidden and system files.

name: Get-ChildItem
title: List directory contents in PowerShell
description: Returns the items in a location as objects rather than text, so results can be filtered and sorted with the pipeline. Aliased to 'ls', 'dir', and 'gci'.

flags.name: -Recurse
flags.description: Include items in all subdirectories.

flags.name: -Force
flags.description: Include hidden and system items.

flags.name: -Filter
flags.description: Filter results by a provider-level wildcard pattern, which is faster than -Include.

examples.explanation: Lists items in the current directory.
Finds every .log file beneath the current directory.

name: Copy-Item
title: Copy files or directories in PowerShell
description: Copies an item from one location to another. Copying a directory tree requires -Recurse; without it only the directory itself is copied.

flags.name: -Recurse
flags.description: Copy a directory and everything inside it.

flags.name: -Force
flags.description: Overwrite existing read-only or hidden destination files.

examples.explanation: Copies a single file to a new name.

risk.sideEffects: Writes new files and can overwrite the destination when -Force is used.
risk.reversibility: Reversible by deleting the copy, unless an existing file was overwritten.

name: du
title: Show disk usage of files and directories
description: Reports how much disk space directories consume. Useful for tracking down what is filling a disk.

flags.name: -h
flags.description: Print sizes in human-readable units such as K, M, and G.

flags.name: -s
flags.description: Show only a total for each argument instead of every subdirectory.

flags.name: -d
flags.description: Limit how many directory levels deep to report.

examples.explanation: Prints the total size of the current directory in human-readable form.
Shows the size of each immediate subdirectory.

risk.sideEffects: Read-only; may be slow on very large trees.

name: df
title: Show free disk space on mounted filesystems
description: Reports total, used, and available space for each mounted filesystem. Answers 'is the disk full?' where 'du' answers 'what is filling it?'.
aliases: how much disk space is left

flags.name: -h
flags.description: Print sizes in human-readable units.

flags.name: -i
flags.description: Report inode usage instead of block usage.

flags.name: -T
flags.description: Include the filesystem type in the output.

examples.explanation: Shows free space per filesystem in human-readable units.

name: ln
title: Create links between files
description: Creates a hard link, or with -s a symbolic link that points at another path. Symbolic links are the common case and can span filesystems.

flags.name: -s
flags.description: Create a symbolic link rather than a hard link.

flags.name: -f
flags.description: Remove an existing destination file before linking.

flags.name: -n
flags.description: Treat an existing symlink to a directory as a file, not as the directory.

examples.explanation: Creates a symbolic link named app pointing at the target path.

risk.sideEffects: Creates a filesystem entry; with -f it can replace an existing file.
risk.reversibility: Reversible by removing the link, which does not affect the target.

name: chown
title: Change file owner and group
description: Changes which user and group own a file or directory. Changing ownership away from yourself can lock you out of the file, and it usually requires root.

flags.name: -R
flags.description: Apply the change recursively to a directory tree.

flags.name: --from
flags.description: Only change ownership when the current owner matches.

examples.explanation: Makes deploy the owner and www-data the group for that directory.

risk.sideEffects: Alters access control; a recursive change on a system path can break running services.
risk.reversibility: Reversible only if you recorded the previous ownership.

name: pushd
title: Change directory and remember the previous one
description: Pushes the current directory onto a stack and changes to a new one. 'popd' returns to where you were, which makes round trips easier than repeated 'cd'.

examples.explanation: Switches to /var/log while remembering the current directory.
Returns to the directory saved by the last pushd.

risk.sideEffects: Changes the shell's working directory only.
